q: Does Mitiq's ZNE / CDR still measurably reduce error when the noise model includes coherent (unitary) errors and readout error, rather than pure depolarizing noise? Fig. 3 uses real IBMQ/Rigetti hardware traces; our replication used idealized Qiskit-Aer depolarizing channels, so the harder failure modes of real devices (coherent Z rotations, T1/T2 imbalance, ZZ crosstalk, readout asymmetry) were never stressed.
basis: Our replication (report/evidence/zne_results.json) used only Qiskit-Aer NoiseModel with depolarizing_error(p1=0.01, p2=0.04). Paper Fig. 3 legend clearly names IBMQ London and Rigetti Aspen-8 as the backends. Mitiq documentation (v1.0.0) also notes that ZNE unitary folding assumes noise is roughly gate-count-proportional, which coherent errors violate.
next_steps: Rebuild the ZNE sweep using Qiskit-Aer's device NoiseModel.from_backend() on a still-public IBMQ backend snapshot (e.g. FakeManilaV2) which bundles readout and thermal-relaxation errors, then repeat with an added deterministic RZ over-rotation of ~2% on every single-qubit gate to inject coherent error. Report the Delta-error-reduction curve for each of Richardson / polynomial / linear as a function of coherent-error amplitude. Free endpoints only: runs locally on CPU.

q: How does the CDR result on a Clifford-dominant circuit compare to the learning-based CDR variants (vnCDR, learning-based Clifford data regression, or the more recent variable-noise CDR) that post-date the 2022 paper? Our replication used only the base CDR; the Mitiq repo has since added these variants, but no head-to-head replication was performed.
basis: Our CDR replication (report/evidence/cdr_results.json) used mitiq.cdr.execute_with_cdr with num_training_circuits=10 and fraction_non_clifford=0.2, which is base CDR (Czarnik et al. 2021). Mitiq 1.0.0's cdr module also exposes vnCDR-style APIs that the 2022 paper's Section 6 mentions only in passing. No direct comparison exists in our evidence set.
next_steps: Add a third script code/cdr_variants.py that runs base CDR, vnCDR (with 2-3 noise scale factors folded into the training set), and a learning-based CDR with a small feed-forward regressor on the same 7-op Cirq circuit. Sweep fraction_non_clifford in {0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6}. Report mitigated-vs-truth error for each variant. Expected outcome: vnCDR should improve on base CDR when the target circuit is further from Clifford; base CDR should dominate at fraction_non_clifford <= 0.2.

q: Would combining ZNE with PEC (as Mitiq now supports via composable executors) yield better mitigation than either alone on our test circuits, and does the paper's implicit claim of composability survive a real numerical test? PEC was not exercised at all in our replication.
basis: REPORT.md §4c explicitly states PEC was not exercised; the paper (§5) treats PEC as a first-class technique but its numerical demonstration is more of a template. Mitiq v1.0.0's pec module and the composable executor pattern advertised in the paper ("framework-agnostic + method-agnostic") make a ZNE+PEC combination a natural test.
next_steps: Write code/pec_replicate.py that runs execute_with_pec on the same depth-8 RB-like circuit family used in the ZNE experiment (needs a quasi-probability representation of the noisy gate set --- Mitiq provides representations.represent_operation_with_local_depolarizing_noise for exactly this). Then write code/zne_pec_combined.py that wraps the PEC-mitigated executor inside execute_with_zne. Compare mean |error| for {raw, ZNE, PEC, ZNE+PEC} on 10 seeds. Free endpoints only.

q: Does the >=40% error reduction we observed for Richardson/polynomial ZNE hold on deeper circuits (depth 20, 40, 80), or does the technique degrade rapidly as the raw noisy signal approaches the fully-mixed floor of 0.25? The paper's Fig. 3 uses fixed shallow circuits; the scaling behavior is not documented.
basis: Our ZNE replication used a single circuit depth (8). The raw noisy value was 0.433, well above the 0.25 mixed-state floor. As depth grows the raw signal will approach 0.25 and the extrapolation target (0) will become increasingly noise-dominated. The Mitiq paper does not chart depth-scaling of the mitigated error in Fig. 3.
next_steps: Parametrize code/zne_replicate.py by depth in {4, 8, 16, 32, 64}, keeping n_seeds=10 and the same noise model. Plot raw noisy, Richardson-ZNE, Polynomial-ZNE, Linear-ZNE mean absolute error vs depth on a single figure. Expected: all mitigated curves should degrade monotonically; identify the depth at which each method crosses the raw noisy baseline (loses its mitigation advantage). Extrapolation methods should degrade at different rates --- linear likely fails first, Richardson last.

q: Can the Mitiq ZNE/CDR results be reproduced on newer real NISQ hardware (e.g. IBM Heron / Kingston, IonQ Forte, Quantinuum H2) that post-dates the 2022 paper, and does the mitigation advantage survive on hardware whose native error rates are 5-10x lower than the 2021 IBMQ London / Rigetti Aspen-8 devices? Or does mitigation become less impactful as raw hardware improves?
basis: Our replication is simulator-only (Qiskit-Aer + Cirq DensityMatrixSimulator). The paper's Fig. 3 hardware panel is fundamentally about the value of mitigation on 2021-era NISQ. Since then, gate fidelities on leading platforms have improved by ~10x (median 2q gate error < 5e-3 on IBM Heron, < 1e-3 on Quantinuum H2). Whether ZNE still yields the same ~40% error reduction on those devices is unknown.
next_steps: Register an IBM Quantum free-tier account (still available for Open Plan users as of 2026) and re-run the exact code/zne_replicate.py script through qiskit_ibm_runtime.SamplerV2 on an ibm_kingston or ibm_torino backend. Use the same 10 random seeds and depth-8 circuits so results are directly comparable to our simulator numbers. Report raw noisy, ZNE-Richardson, and Delta as before. Constraint: free tier throttles to ~10 min/month; keep to <=30 total circuit executions. Do NOT use paid QPUs. If free-tier hardware access is unavailable, fall back to Qiskit-Aer with NoiseModel.from_backend(FakeKingston()).
